macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Tech-led selloff pressures Wall Street
items.summary: U.S. stocks ended lower, with the Dow down 0.25%, the S&P 500 down 0.30%, and the Nasdaq Composite down 1.37%. Alphabet’s sharp decline revived concerns that massive AI spending may not generate adequate returns.[15]

items.title: U.S. stock futures fall as Amazon and Intel disappoint
items.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures fell more than 2%, while Amazon dropped about 7% and Intel plunged roughly 23% in premarket trading. Amazon’s weaker results and higher planned capital spending, alongside Intel’s weak outlook and expected cash burn, intensified concerns about the cost of the AI buildout.[14][17]

items.title: Alphabet shares suffer record-scale decline
items.summary: Alphabet fell about 12.6% after disappointing search and advertising performance and rising AI-related cash outflows, wiping out approximately $500 billion in market value. The results intensified investor scrutiny of technology companies’ AI investment returns.[16]

items.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady
items.summary: The Fed left its policy rate unchanged and said it needed to accumulate more information while inflation remained elevated. The decision provided no firm signal on when another rate move might occur.[15]

items.title: ECB and Bank of Japan also maintain rates
items.summary: The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan kept policy unchanged this week. The BoJ maintained its benchmark rate at 1.25%, while the ECB left open the possibility of a December increase if inflation pressures persist.[12][4]

items.title: U.S. GDP grows faster than expected
items.summary: U.S. third-quarter GDP expanded at a 3.4% annualized rate, exceeding the 3.2% expectation, supported by consumer spending and AI-related investment. The stronger data reinforced concerns that interest rates could remain high for longer.[1][20]

items.title: U.S. inflation remains elevated
items.summary: The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.6% in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and meeting expectations. The data added to market concerns about persistent price pressures.[2]

items.title: Microsoft and SK Hynix report strong results
items.summary: Microsoft delivered a strong cash-flow result and robust cloud-growth outlook, while SK Hynix reported quarterly profit more than seven times higher than a year earlier. Microsoft shares rose in extended trading and SK Hynix gained 13%.[11]

items.title: Investors shift toward government bonds
items.summary: Technology-sector losses and uncertainty over AI spending fueled a defensive move into bonds, pushing U.S. Treasury yields lower and putting bonds on track for their strongest monthly gain in nearly three years.[14]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance reports suspected $6.3 billion security breach
items.summary: Binance said a compromised DevOps engineer laptop may have enabled attackers to drain roughly $6.3 billion across multiple blockchains. Tether and Circle reportedly froze substantial amounts of the stolen assets, while TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor.[1][2][3]

items.title: Crypto market falls as Binance incident triggers liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell to about $76,300 and later traded near $78,273, down 2.48% over 24 hours. Total crypto liquidations reportedly reached approximately $943.5 million as the overall market capitalization declined 4.26%.[2][3]

items.title: ICE and Trade[XYZ] plan regulated U.S. perpetual-futures market
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is partnering with Hyperliquid builder Trade[XYZ] to develop a KYC- and AML-compliant perpetual-futures market for crypto and traditional assets, subject to CFTC approval.[4]

items.title: CoinDCX restricts new futures positions after Binance disruption
items.summary: Indian exchange CoinDCX temporarily placed its futures market in reduce-only mode, citing developments affecting global liquidity providers. The restriction prevents traders from opening or increasing futures positions while allowing management of existing positions.[5]

items.title: XRP Ledger developers propose restricted-token safeguards
items.summary: XRP Ledger developers proposed four fixes to prevent restricted tokens from entering accounts without issuer approval. The changes are part of the proposed fixCleanup3_5_0 upgrade, which has not yet activated on mainnet.[5]

items.title: U.S. Treasury sanctions North Korea-linked crypto facilitators
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity accused of facilitating North Korean IT-worker fraud that funnels cryptocurrency proceeds into weapons programs.[6]

items.title: Bank of England consults on tokenized collateral
items.summary: The Bank of England opened a consultation on allowing central counterparties to accept tokenized collateral in clearing, proposing a regulatory framework ahead of a February 2027 implementation deadline.[6]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for Large 4
items.summary: Mistral released the open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter Large 4 model, claiming improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity. The model reportedly leads Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 and scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index.

items.title: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon leads new AI benchmark rankings
items.summary: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon reportedly reached the top of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59 and strong cybersecurity performance. Google is initially making it available to cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program.

items.title: GitHub unveils Copilot Fusion and expanded agent tools
items.summary: At GitHub Universe 2026, GitHub announced Copilot Fusion and additional software-development agent capabilities. Enterprise customers can also pay for AI credits rather than traditional Copilot seats.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind’s Genie 4 reportedly generates playable worlds with native sound, dialogue, and live steering, extending the capabilities demonstrated by Genie 3.

items.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3 multimodal models
items.summary: Liquid AI released LFM3, a family of six multimodal models of roughly 2 billion parameters built on a shared backbone and pretrained on 22 trillion tokens.

items.title: Circuit Mind raises $25 million for AI circuit design
items.summary: London-based Circuit Mind raised $25 million across a Norwest-led Series A and an earlier seed round. Its AI tools convert block diagrams into circuit-board schematics, with customers reporting design cycles shortened from months to weeks.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
items.summary: NVIDIA released an open-weight speech model that transcribes recordings in 40 languages, translates them, and identifies speakers according to user instructions.

items.title: Anthropic adds self-assessment monitoring to Claude
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly added a system in which Claude assesses conversation risks immediately after responding. The company says the system detects most high-risk conversations while adding less than 2% to inference costs.

items.title: Anthropic prepares IPO filing
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly filed an S-1 registration statement this week in preparation for an initial public offering, according to reporting summarized by The Zvi Mowshowitz newsletter.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero launches to major Steam debut
items.summary: S-Game’s kung-fu action game Phantom Blade Zero launched on Windows and PlayStation 5, reportedly exceeding 723,000 concurrent Steam players and topping the platform’s global best-seller chart.[1]

items.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders releases on mobile
items.summary: Tencent’s TiMi Studio Group and Capcom released Monster Hunter Outlanders for mobile, featuring redesigned controls, a new storyline, and shorter play sessions for phone users.[2]

items.title: Netflix developing live-action PUBG series
items.summary: Krafton announced a Netflix live-action adaptation of PUBG, with Donald Glover attached to direct, write, executive-produce, and star.[3]

items.title: The Duskbloods delayed to 2027
items.summary: FromSoftware postponed the Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods to 2027 following its network test.[3]

items.title: PHP vulnerability disrupts multiple online games
items.summary: A PHP vulnerability reportedly caused outages affecting games including Final Fantasy XIV and Umamusume: Pretty Derby, disrupting services across multiple regions.[4]

items.title: Lords of the Fallen II pushed to early 2027
items.summary: CI Games moved Lords of the Fallen II from 2026 to the first quarter of 2027 and delayed its closed beta to January.[2]

items.title: GameMaker commercial PC licensing to become free
items.summary: YoYo Games said GameMaker’s next-generation runtime will be free for commercial desktop use beginning January 1, 2027, removing the need for a Professional license on supported platforms.[5]
